title: Beginner calisthenics For Big Guys
author: B D.
desc:
Here's a revised 3-day a week workout plan with exercises that focus on building a strong, durable, and aesthetic body while addressing lower back pain and developing round glutes and shoulders. Each exercise includes the muscle groups targeted, instructions for proper form, and sets/reps.

Day 1: Upper Body Strength and Core Stability
Focus on building pushing and pulling strength for your chest, shoulders, back, and core.

Day 2: Lower Body (Glute-Focused) and Core
Focus on strengthening glutes, hamstrings, quads, and core to improve back stability and build rounder glutes.

Day 3: Functional Full-Body Strength
Emphasize functional movements to improve coordination, posture, and overall strength.

Why This Plan Works for You:

Glutes and Shoulders: Hip thrusts, Bulgarian split squats, clamshells, and lateral band walks build round glutes, while pike push-ups, ring push-ups, and wall angels target shoulder aesthetics and strength.

Core and Back Health: Bird dogs, hollow holds, and side planks stabilize your spine, preventing back pain.
Foundation for Advanced Moves: Builds strength for future progressions like pistol squats.

Balanced Muscle Development: Ensures every major muscle group is targeted for a functional and aesthetic physique.

Duration and Progression:
Follow for 8-12 weeks.
Track your reps, sets, and form. Gradually increase difficulty by:
Adding weight to lower-body exercises.
Reducing assistance on pull-ups.
Increasing time under tension (e.g., holding planks or carries longer).

ex.note:
Adjust rings to about waist height.
Grab the rings with an overhand grip, feet extended forward.

Keep your body straight, pull your chest toward the rings, and squeeze your shoulder blades.

Set rings slightly higher than waist height.
Lean into the rings, keeping your body straight, and lower yourself into a push-up position.
Push back up while keeping your core tight.

Start in a downward dog position, hands shoulder-width apart, hips raised high.
Lower your head toward the floor, bending at the elbows.
Push back up to the starting position.

Lie on your side with your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips to form a straight line from head to heels.
Hold, then switch sides.

Stand with your back against a wall, feet a few inches away, lower back touching the wall.
Raise your arms into a "goalpost" position and slide them up and down the wall while maintaining contact.

Sit with your upper back against a bench, feet flat on the floor.
Drive your hips up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower back down in a controlled motion.

Add weight when ready

Place one foot behind you on a low surface (ring or bench).
Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.

Lie on your back with your feet in the rings or on a stability ball.
Curl your feet toward your hips while lifting your hips.
Lower back down slowly.

Use band if available.

Lie on your side with your knees bent at 90 degrees.
Open your top knee while keeping your feet together.
Slowly lower the knee back down.

Start on all fours, keeping your spine neutral.
Extend one arm and the opposite leg, keeping your hips stable.
Return to the starting position and switch sides.

(Or pull up negatives)

Use a resistance band or box to assist.
Pull your chin above the rings, focusing on squeezing your back.
Lower down slowly.

Hold a weight (if available) at chest level or perform bodyweight squats.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to standing.

Lie on your back with your arms and legs extended.
Lift your shoulders and legs slightly off the ground, keeping your lower back pressed down.

Hold weights at your sides and walk in a straight line.
Keep your core tight and shoulders back.

Place a resistance band around your thighs.
Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Repeat in the opposite direction.
